claim: Neither FL-BubR1 nor BubR1ΔI overexpression permitted an arrest longer than that observed in wild-type MEFs in checkpoint silencing assays.
source: In this assay, neither FL-BubR1 nor BubR1ΔI overexpression permitted an arrest longer than that observed in wild-type MEFs.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 5B.

claim: PP2A localization was normal in BubR1ΔI overexpressing cells.
source: We found PP2A localization to be normal in BubR1ΔI overexpressing cells, suggesting this branch of signaling is not impacted (Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by immunostaining data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The threshold to engage the SAC is lowered by the Bub1bΔI transgene.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that the threshold to engage the SAC is instead lowered by the Bub1bΔI transgene.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the SAC activation and silencing data.

claim: Overexpression of FL-BubR1 lead to increased interaction of BubR1 and Cdc20.
source: We found that overexpression of FL-BubR1 lead to increased interaction of BubR1 and Cdc20, as had been previously shown (Figure 6A) (Baker et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by co-IP data in Figure 6A and a citation to Baker et al., 2013.

claim: There were an increased amount of complexes consisting of BubR1-Cdc20-Mad2 in FL-Bub1b MEFs.
source: This was confirmed by Cdc20 and Mad2 co-IPs and subsequent analysis of co-precipitating proteins (Figure 6B,C) that indicated there were an increased amount of complexes consisting of BubR1-Cdc20-Mad2, a potent APC/C inhibitor.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by co-IP data in Figure 6B,C.

claim: BubR1-Cdc20-Mad2 is a potent APC/C inhibitor.
source: This was confirmed by Cdc20 and Mad2 co-IPs and subsequent analysis of co-precipitating proteins (Figure 6B,C) that indicated there were an increased amount of complexes consisting of BubR1-Cdc20-Mad2, a potent APC/C inhibitor.
evidence: This is stated in the text as an established fact.

claim: While the total amount of BubR1 (wild-type and mutant) immunoprecipitated in Bub1bΔI MEFs is increased substantially over normal MEFs, BubR1 lacking the internal Cdc20-binding domain failed to pull-down excess Cdc20 and vice versa.
source: However, we found that while the total amount of BubR1 (wild-type and mutant) immunoprecipitated in Bub1bΔI MEFs is increased substantially over normal MEFs, BubR1 lacking the internal Cdc20-binding domain failed to pull-down excess Cdc20 and vice versa (Figure 6A,C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by co-IP data in Figure 6A,C.

claim: While BubR1ΔI can likely bind to Cdc20, it is not a preferred partner.
source: This suggests that while BubR1ΔI can likely bind to Cdc20, it is not a preferred partner.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the co-IP data.

claim: The amount of Mad2 co-precipitated by Cdc20 was increased in Bub1bΔI MEFs, indicating that a larger proportion of Cdc20 bound Mad2 than in wild-type MEFs.
source: Surprisingly, the amount of Mad2 co-precipitated by Cdc20 was increased, indicating that a larger proportion of Cdc20 bound Mad2 than in wild-type MEFs, while retaining similar levels of BubR1-Cdc20-Mad2 complexes as wild-type.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by co-IP data in Figure 6.

claim: Bub1bΔI MEFs retain similar levels of BubR1-Cdc20-Mad2 complexes as wild-type.
source: Surprisingly, the amount of Mad2 co-precipitated by Cdc20 was increased, indicating that a larger proportion of Cdc20 bound Mad2 than in wild-type MEFs, while retaining similar levels of BubR1-Cdc20-Mad2 complexes as wild-type.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by co-IP data in Figure 6.

claim: The unique MCC compositions in Bub1bΔI MEFs did not result from changes to total levels of MCC proteins.
source: These unique MCC compositions did not result from changes to total levels of these proteins (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: FL-BubR1 overexpression results in the ability for cells to form more mitotic checkpoint complexes compared to wild-type MEFs, which can likely fortify the SAC signaling potential.
source: Thus, FL-BubR1 overexpression alone results in the ability for cells to form more mitotic checkpoint complexes compared to wild-type MEFs, which can likely fortify the SAC signaling potential.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the co-IP data showing increased MCC formation.

claim: The levels of phosphorylation of Cdc20 S153 and S92 were equivalent to wild-type MEFs in FL-Bub1b and Bub1bΔI MEFs.
source: We found the levels of phosphorylation of both these residues to be equivalent to wild-type MEFs, suggesting this method of APC/C control is not hyperactive in our mutants.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 6D.

claim: FL-BubR1 and BubR1ΔI both significantly blunted the increase in syntelic attachments caused by hypoactive Aurora B.
source: FL-BubR1 and BubR1ΔI both significantly blunted the increase in syntelic attachments caused by hypoactive Aurora B (Figure 7).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by monastrol washout data in Figure 7.

claim: No corrective effects on syntelic attachments were observed in the Bub1bΔN or Bub1bN mutants.
source: In contrast, no such corrective effects were observed in the Bub1bΔN or Bub1bN mutants.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: Overexpression of BubR1∆I provided a similar extension to the metaphase-to-anaphase transition as MEFs derived from Bub1b∆I transgenic mice.
source: Overexpression of BubR1∆I provided a similar extension to the metaphase-to-anaphase transition as MEFs derived from Bub1b∆I transgenic mice.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 9A.

claim: None of the other deletion constructs (Bub1b∆Phe, Bub1b∆D, Bub1b∆KARD, Bub1b∆PheD∆KARD) changed the duration of mitosis when overexpressed.
source: However, none of the other deletion constructs changed the duration of mitosis when overexpressed.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 9A and Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: An unmapped domain within residues 525–700 regulates mitotic timing.
source: Again, no extended mitotic timing was observed, implying that an unmapped domain within residues 525–700 regulates mitotic timing.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the mitotic timing data of various deletion mutants.

claim: BubR1∆I-expressing MEFs showed the most profound increase in the duration of nocodazole-mediated arrest.
source: As expected, BubR1∆I-expressing MEFs showed the most profound increase in the duration of nocodazole-mediated arrest
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 9B.

claim: FL-BubR1 overexpression caused a moderate, but significant increase in nocodazole arrest duration.
source: while FL-BubR1 overexpression caused a moderate, but significant increase (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 9B.

claim: Bub1b∆Phe, Bub1b∆D and Bub1b∆KARD behaved like overexpression of FL-BubR1 in nocodazole arrest assays.
source: Of our newly generated mutants, Bub1b∆Phe, Bub1b∆D and Bub1b∆KARD behaved like overexpression of FL-BubR1
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 9B.

claim: Bub1b∆PheD phenocopied Bub1b∆I in nocodazole arrest assays.
source: while Bub1b∆PheD phenocopied Bub1b∆I.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 9B.

claim: None of the individual domains (Phe box, D-box2, KARD) is required for SAC reinforcement by high levels of BubR1.
source: These findings indicate that none of the individual domains is required for SAC reinforcement by high levels of BubR1
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the nocodazole arrest data of various deletion mutants.

claim: The combinatorial loss of both the Phe and D-box2 motifs is a requirement for robust checkpoint sustainability.
source: and the combinatorial loss of both the Phe and D-box2 motifs is a requirement for robust checkpoint sustainability.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the nocodazole arrest data showing that Bub1b∆PheD phenocopies Bub1b∆I.

claim: All mutants (Bub1b∆Phe, Bub1b∆D, Bub1b∆KARD, Bub1b∆PheD) improved microtubule-kinetochore attachment error correction to a similar extent as FL-BubR1.
source: When examined for the ability to improve microtubule-kinetochore attachment error correction in monastrol washout assays with and without Aurora B inhibition, all mutants did so to a similar extent as FL-BubR1 (Figure 9C)
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by monastrol washout data in Figure 9C.

claim: Individual domains within the 525–700 region are not required for SAC and error correction reinforcement by BubR1 overexpression.
source: Altogether, our studies using refined BubR1ΔI mutants indicate that individual domains within the 525–700 region are not required for SAC and error correction reinforcement by BubR1 overexpression
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data on various deletion mutants.

claim: Maximal SAC reinforcement is achieved when both internal Cdc20-binding motifs (Phe box and D-box2) are absent.
source: and that maximal SAC reinforcement is achieved when both internal Cdc20-binding motifs are absent.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing that Bub1b∆PheD phenocopies Bub1b∆I.

claim: Ectopic expression of KrasG12V had no impact on timing of mitosis.
source: We found that ectopic expression of KrasG12V had no impact on timing of mitosis and SAC signaling (Figure 10A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by live cell imaging data in Figure 10A-C.

claim: Ectopic expression of KrasG12V had no impact on SAC signaling.
source: We found that ectopic expression of KrasG12V had no impact on timing of mitosis and SAC signaling (Figure 10A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by live cell imaging data in Figure 10A-C.

claim: In monastrol washout assays, KrasG12V-expressing MEFs produced significantly higher rates of misaligned chromosomes over empty vector alone.
source: On the other hand, in monastrol washout assays, KrasG12V-expressing MEFs produced significantly higher rates of misaligned chromosomes over empty vector alone (Figure 10D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by monastrol washout data in Figure 10D.

claim: KrasG12V-expressing MEFs showed a remarkable increase in misaligned chromosomes in live cell imaging experiments.
source: In complementary experiments in which we monitored chromosome segregation errors by live cell imaging, KrasG12V-expressing MEFs showed a remarkable increase in misaligned chromosomes (Figure 10E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by live cell imaging data in Figure 10E.

claim: Oncogenic Kras cells may be particularly prone to syntelic attachments.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that oncogenic Kras cells may be particularly prone to syntelic attachments.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing increased misalignments in KrasG12V-expressing MEFs.

claim: Overexpression of a mutant BubR1 that includes disruptions of the internal Cdc20-binding domain (BubR1∆I) elicits a tumor-protective mechanism similar to that of full-length (FL)-BubR1 overexpression.
source: We show that overexpression of a mutant BubR1 that includes disruptions of the internal Cdc20-binding domain (BubR1∆I) elicits a tumor-protective mechanism similar to that of full-length (FL)-BubR1 overexpression.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Discussion and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Like FL-Bub1b, overexpression of BubR1∆I safeguards against aneuploidization, likely by both strengthening SAC signaling and preventing improper KT-MT attachments.
source: Importantly, like in FL-Bub1b, overexpression of this mutant also safeguards against aneuploidization, likely by both strengthening SAC signaling and preventing improper KT-MT attachments.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Discussion and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: The internal Cdc20-binding domain is dispensable to mediate the protective effects of BubR1 overexpression against aneuploidy and cancer.
source: Thus, the internal Cdc20-binding domain is dispensable to mediate these protective effects
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Discussion and supported by experimental data showing that BubR1∆I protects against aneuploidy and cancer.

claim: The N-terminal Cdc20-binding domain is necessary, but not sufficient for the protective effects of BubR1 overexpression.
source: while the N-terminal Cdc20-binding domain is necessary, but not sufficient.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Discussion and supported by experimental data showing that BubR1N does not protect against aneuploidy and cancer.

claim: BubR1∆I provides distinct molecular properties unique to that of overexpression alone that also likely promote genetic stability and show no overt detrimental effects on cells or mice.
source: BubR1∆I also provides distinct molecular properties unique to that of overexpression alone that also likely promote genetic stability and show no overt detrimental effects on cells or mice.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by experimental data showing unique properties of BubR1∆I.

claim: BubR1∆I overexpression results in a more robust SAC that is more responsive to weak stimuli.
source: This includes a more robust SAC that is more responsive to weak stimuli
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by experimental data in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: BubR1∆I overexpression results in an increase in the normal length of mitosis.
source: and an increase in the normal length of mitosis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by experimental data in Figure 4.

claim: A maximal SAC response can be achieved exclusively by the loss of the Phe box and D-box2.
source: With further refined mutant Bub1b constructs, we demonstrate that a maximal SAC response can be achieved exclusively by the loss of the Phe box and D-box2
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by experimental data in Figure 9.

claim: The mitotic timing may be dependent on previously uncharacterized regions of BubR1.
source: and that the mitotic timing may be dependent on previously uncharacterized regions of BubR1.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and is an inference drawn from the mitotic timing data of various deletion mutants.

claim: Enhancing genomic stability fortifies the barriers of transformation.
source: Importantly, this work sheds light on the causal role of CIN in cancer by demonstrating that enhancing genomic stability fortifies the barriers of transformation
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion based on the overall findings of the study.
